engine_rules.name: Enforce Alternate Picking Stroke Equality
engine_rules.falsifier: Upstroke produces measurably weaker dynamic than downstroke
engine_rules.anchor: strive to make up strokes sound as strong as down strokes

engine_rules.name: Restrict to Eighth Notes in Phase 1
engine_rules.falsifier: Any non-eighth subdivision, rest, hammer-on, or pull-off appears in weeks 1–13
engine_rules.anchor: Play only eighth notes, continuous and uninterrupted. No rests. No phrasing. No hammer-on's. No pull-offts. No other ornamentation.

engine_rules.name: Unlock Legato Techniques at Week 15
engine_rules.falsifier: Legato devices introduced before week 15
engine_rules.anchor: via these devices several notes can be produced with one picking stroke

engine_rules.name: Apply Whole-Tone Scale Over Dominant 7th
engine_rules.falsifier: Scale contains a half step
engine_rules.anchor: The Whole Tone Scale (symetrical, consecutive whole steps) most commonly used over dominant 7th chords.

engine_rules.name: Apply Diminished Scale Over Dominant 7th for Tension
engine_rules.falsifier: Scale does not alternate whole and half steps symmetrically
engine_rules.anchor: The Diminished Scale (symetrical, consecutive whole step and half steps) most commonly used over dominant 7th chords or diminished chords.

engine_rules.name: Use Major Pentatonic Over Major 6/9 Context
engine_rules.falsifier: Scale includes the 4th or 7th degree
engine_rules.anchor: The Major Pentatonic Scale (same as diatonic major with the active tones 3rd and 7th left out). When harmonized creates inversions of a Major 6/9 chord

engine_rules.name: Navigate by Key Center Not Chord-by-Chord
engine_rules.falsifier: Improviser treats each chord as an independent harmonic target rather than a member of a key center
engine_rules.anchor: for each new one, move your hand to a convenient fingering pattern for that particular scale and do your improvising in that region of the guitar.

engine_rules.name: Use Dominant 7th as Key Center Identifier
engine_rules.falsifier: Dominant 7th chord resolves ambiguously to more than one key center
engine_rules.anchor: Eb 7 is a V chord (Dominant 7 type) which only appears once in any given major key, always as the V chord

engine_rules.name: Use Five Movable Patterns for Full Neck Coverage
engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than five patterns are learned for a given key, leaving fingerboard regions uncovered
engine_rules.anchor: There are five such patterns for any given scale. And each of these five are movable up or down the neck to the selected key

engine_rules.name: Connect Patterns with Exactly Three Move Types
engine_rules.falsifier: A fourth transition method is employed that is not a position skip, stretch, or half-step slide
engine_rules.anchor: There are essentially three 'moves' involved in moving from one pattern to another.

engine_rules.name: Play Arpeggios Within Scale Pattern
engine_rules.falsifier: Arpeggio is played as an isolated chord shape outside the key-center scale pattern
engine_rules.anchor: arpeggios will be easier to handle if they are played within a scale pattern that corresponds to the key center from which the chord is derived

engine_rules.name: Cap Consecutive Scalar Tones at 3-4
engine_rules.falsifier: More than 4 consecutive scale tones appear in the same direction without a skip or direction change
engine_rules.anchor: don't play more than 3 or 4 scale tones in the same direction

engine_rules.name: Derive Interval Skips Diatonically
engine_rules.falsifier: Interval sequence produces parallel (non-diatonic) intervals that ignore the key's half steps
engine_rules.anchor: playing scale intervals that take into account the half steps of the scale

engine_rules.name: Use Common Tones as Line Relief
engine_rules.falsifier: No note is shared between consecutive chords making common-tone sustain harmonically invalid
engine_rules.anchor: The line can be flattened out --- a nice relief from excessive vertical movement.

engine_rules.name: Use Arpeggios to Contrast Scale Movement
engine_rules.falsifier: Arpeggio used consecutively with another arpeggio without any intervening scalar motion
engine_rules.anchor: Arpeggios are specifically chords, broken up into single notes. They are effective in outlining the bar harmony and offer a nice contrast to scale movement

engine_rules.name: Use Large Interval Skips for Dramatic Lines
engine_rules.falsifier: Interval skip is a step (2nd) rather than a skip of a 3rd or larger
engine_rules.anchor: Large interval skips can be a valuable tool for creating interesting lines and can have a dramatic effect

engine_rules.name: Derive Harmonic Minor by Raising 5th Degree of Diatonic Pattern
engine_rules.falsifier: Harmonic minor is learned as an entirely new fingering independent of diatonic major patterns
engine_rules.anchor: the relative harmonic minor scales can be quickly learned by simply sharping the fifth scale step of the diatonic scales

engine_rules.name: Prioritize Bar Harmony Over Melodic Minor Ascending Rule
engine_rules.falsifier: Bar harmony is absent and ascending/descending rules are the only contextual guide
engine_rules.anchor: The ascending and descending rules here are a technicality, which in the final analysis may be disregarded in favor of the existant bar harmony

engine_rules.name: Ear is Final Harmonic Arbiter for Substitutions
engine_rules.falsifier: A substitution is accepted on theoretical grounds alone without an aural check
engine_rules.anchor: If they're right, they will sound right and if they're wrong, you will know it immediately.

engine_rules.name: Treat Key-Center Brackets as One Valid Analysis
engine_rules.falsifier: Only a single key-center reading is considered with no alternative interpretations explored
engine_rules.anchor: The key centers bracketed in the chord progressions represent only one analysis of the progression. Other views may be applied as well

engine_rules.name: Couple Visual Pattern Imprint with Sound
engine_rules.falsifier: Pattern is learned visually only without internalized sound association
engine_rules.anchor: develop a strong visual imprint of the pattern itself, coupled with the tone sequence it produces (the sound)

engine_rules.name: Never Sacrifice Accuracy for Tempo
engine_rules.falsifier: Tempo is increased while note clarity or synchronization errors remain present
engine_rules.anchor: Care should be taken not to sacrifice accuracy and precision in order to meet the tempo goals.

engine_rules.name: Use Metronome as Progress Tracker Not Target
engine_rules.falsifier: Metronome is set to a desired future tempo and player attempts to match it
engine_rules.anchor: Do not set your metronome to a desired speed and try to rise to meet it. Rather, use the metronome only to track your progress.

engine_rules.name: Maintain Tempo 21 Days for Permanent Imprinting
engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than 21 consecutive daily sessions are completed at a given tempo level
engine_rules.anchor: once you reach a given level of speed, and maintain playing at that level or faster, for approximately 21 days, on a daily basis, -- the ability acquired during that period of time will be permanently imprinted

engine_rules.name: Maintain Flexible Right-Hand Technique
engine_rules.falsifier: Right hand is anchored at elbow, wrist, or pick guard in a way that restricts movement
engine_rules.anchor: flexibility-the ability to adapt the right hand to a variety of moves-is the key to longevity.

engine_rules.name: Avoid Fixed Right-Hand Anchor Systems
engine_rules.falsifier: Anchor does not restrict picking range at faster tempos
engine_rules.anchor: avoid is any kind of anchor system that inhibits freedom of movement.

engine_rules.name: Eliminate Flams via Simultaneous Hand Attack
engine_rules.falsifier: Left and right hand attacks are not simultaneous, producing two audible events per note
engine_rules.anchor: the left and right hands must be in perfect synchronization. No Flams!

engine_rules.name: Begin Every Session with 5-Minute Slow Warm-Up
engine_rules.falsifier: Session begins without any slow full-fingerboard warm-up
engine_rules.anchor: At the beginning of each practice session, warm up for 5 minutes by playing notes all over the fingerboard. Play very slowly

engine_rules.name: Fret Strings Perpendicular to Fingerboard
engine_rules.falsifier: Finger contacts string at an oblique angle, shifting string from center
engine_rules.anchor: The fingers should operate straight up and down on the strings, like hammers in a piano, at a right angle to the fingerboard.

engine_rules.name: Minimize Left-Hand Finger Lift
engine_rules.falsifier: Fingers lifted conspicuously higher than needed to clear the string
engine_rules.anchor: The fingers should be lifted only high enough off the string to avoid string noise when moving

engine_rules.name: Maintain Flat Left-Wrist Posture
engine_rules.falsifier: Wrist is severely arched, creating strain or limiting finger mobility
engine_rules.anchor: The wrist should maintain a fairly flat posture. Avoid severe arching of the left wrist

engine_rules.name: Use Minimum .012 First String Gauge
engine_rules.falsifier: First string is lighter than .012
engine_rules.anchor: use a medium-heavy set of strings; nothing smaller than an .012 first string

engine_rules.name: Use Medium-Sized Medium-to-Heavy Celluloid Pick
engine_rules.falsifier: Pick is very large, oddly shaped, or thin
engine_rules.anchor: Your pick should be of medium size, and medium to heavy in thickness. Avoid very large or odd shaped picks. Standard celluloid picks are well suited to this purpose.

engine_rules.name: Require Metronome, Recorder, and Timer
engine_rules.falsifier: Any one of the three tools is absent from the practice setup
engine_rules.anchor: Also essential to the studies in this book will be: (1) a metronome, (2) a reel-to-reel or cassette tape recorder, and (3) an alarm clock or timer.

engine_rules.name: Use Question-and-Answer as Primary Structural Form
engine_rules.falsifier: Line proceeds without any phrase-response relationship
engine_rules.anchor: A very common form for building a solo line is: QUESTION AND ANSWER.

engine_rules.name: Vocalize Line Before Executing on Instrument
engine_rules.falsifier: Player executes a line on instrument without any prior internal or vocal conception
engine_rules.anchor: Listen to the 'pre-recorded changes' and sing the solo the way [you want to play it].

engine_rules.name: Sketch Structural Melody to Scaffold Improvisation
engine_rules.falsifier: No simple structural melody is present to anchor the improvised fills
engine_rules.anchor: sketch out a very simple melody line over the changes, i.e. half note, quarter notes, halves, etc. Let this line run through your head as a basic melody and play 'fills' around it.

engine_rules.name: Memorize Chord Changes Before Improvising
engine_rules.falsifier: Player improvises while reading chord symbols from notation
engine_rules.anchor: Get the progression off the paper and into your head as soon as possible.

engine_rules.name: Practice 50 Minutes Six Days Per Week
engine_rules.falsifier: Session shorter than 50 minutes or fewer than 6 days practiced in a week without injury
engine_rules.anchor: The Program is made up of a series of project lessons, each lasting 50 minutes per day, running six consecutive days per week, with one day off.

engine_rules.name: Execute Three Phases in Strict Sequence
engine_rules.falsifier: A later phase technique (triplets, legato) is introduced before its designated week range
engine_rules.anchor: The First Six Weeks ... focus on the use of eighth notes ... Weeks Eight Through Thirteen ... focus on triple time via eighth note triplets.

engine_rules.name: Never Skip a Practice Day
engine_rules.falsifier: A day is skipped for any reason during the program
engine_rules.anchor: Avoid skipping a day, for whatever reason. The effect is hazardous to progress. Regularity is essential.

engine_rules.name: Transpose Lessons to New Keys for Creative Stimulus
engine_rules.falsifier: Lesson is repeated in the same key without transposition
engine_rules.anchor: Project Lesson 1-B uses the same chord progression transposed to another key, thus requiring a change of fingering patterns, licks, etc.

engine_rules.name: Prioritize Group Practice as Phase Accelerator
engine_rules.falsifier: Group practice is available but solo practice is chosen instead
engine_rules.anchor: The group dynamics is superior to private study for a program of this sort.

engine_rules.name: Treat All Technique as Servant of Spontaneous Invention
engine_rules.falsifier: Model solo examples are reproduced verbatim rather than used as reference
engine_rules.anchor: The important consideration is the spontaneous invention of your own solo line.

engine_rules.name: Break Repeated Licks in Real Time Without Stopping
engine_rules.falsifier: Player stops playing to reconsider rather than varying in the flow
engine_rules.anchor: Be aware of this point in the tune and the next time around, do something else, no stops.

engine_rules.name: Play Legato and Hold Steady Time
engine_rules.falsifier: Notes are clipped short or tempo wavers measurably from the metronome click
engine_rules.anchor: Play Legato. Hold each note as long as possible. Great attention should be given to holding steady time. Do not rush or drag the tempo.
